title: Joint neutrino oscillation analysis from the T2K and NOvA experiments

date.note: Published as Nature 646, 818-824 (2025); posted to arXiv the same day (2510.19888).

claim.quote: Here, we carry out the first joint analysis of data sets from NOvA and T2K, the two currently operating long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments (hundreds of kilometers of neutrino travel distance), taking advantage of our complementary experimental designs and setting new constraints on several neutrino sector parameters.

summary.plain: NOvA and T2K, the two operating long-distance neutrino experiments, combined their data for the first time. Together they pin down how the masses of the three neutrino types differ from each other more precisely than either experiment could alone.
summary.technical: First joint three-flavor oscillation fit of NOvA and T2K neutrino- and antineutrino-mode data sets, exploiting the experiments' different baselines and beam energies to break parameter degeneracies. Reports |Δm²₃₂| = 2.43+0.04/-0.03 (normal ordering) or -2.48+0.03/-0.04 (inverted ordering) ×10⁻³ eV², and a 3σ interval on δ_CP of [-1.38π, 0.30π] (normal) / [-0.92π, -0.04π] (inverted); no strong preference for mass ordering is found.

why_it_matters: The first combination of the world's two currently running long-baseline accelerator neutrino experiments, giving the most precise joint constraint yet on the neutrino mass-squared splitting and narrowing the allowed range for the CP-violating phase δ_CP.

key_value.note: Unit recorded as eV^2 (an energy-squared quantity); the ontology's `energy` dimension list has no eV^2 unit, so this value is informational and not asserted against the dimension whitelist. Inverted-ordering value is -2.48(+0.03/-0.04)×10⁻³ eV².
